title: Digital Shadow for Squirrel-Cage Induction Motors: Real-Time Loss Estimation and ANFIS-Based Fault Detection
content: This paper presents a digital shadow framework for squirrel cage induction motors in Industry 4.0. Sensor data flow automatically from the physical motor to its virtual representation. The virtual model estimates losses and efficiency without sending control commands to the drive. The framework combines an enhanced double cage equivalent circuit with five Sugeno ANFIS models. These models estimate stator copper losses, core losses, rotor copper losses, mechanical losses, and stray load losses. Motor parameters are identified offline from a database of 60 motor nameplate datasets using a genetic algorithm and MATLAB FSOLVE. A three dimensional thermal analysis is performed in MATLAB PDE Toolbox using geometry exported from SolidWorks. The circuit model supplies the volumetric heat sources. A resistive thermal network provides a reduced thermal model. Experiments on a 1.5 kW motor use a centrifugal pump profile and a biscuit conveyor profile. The reported test RMSE remains below 1.8 W for all five loss components. The maximum reported efficiency tracking error is 0.6 percentage points. The framework also detects broken rotor bars by tracking loss components and efficiency. The classifier correctly identifies all 420 test operating points across five configurations with zero to four broken bars. These results apply to the tested operating conditions and support further evaluation of the framework for industrial monitoring and fault diagnosis.
